Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the VitalCore Medical Devices third quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO; Michael Chen, CFO; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. VitalCore Medical Devices delivered solid results this quarter, driven by strong execution and continued demand for our innovative medical device solutions.

Today, I will cover four key aspects of our performance. First, our new product launches and their contribution to growth. Second, gross margin trends along with supply chain updates. Third, the evolving mix between capital equipment and consumables. And fourth, the impact of our pricing and cost management initiatives.

Michael will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with our new product launches and their outsized role in driving growth. In the medical devices sector, where innovation fuels long-term revenue expansion—especially as procedural volumes stabilize in areas like orthopedics and structural heart—our recently launched portfolio has been a game-changer. Products introduced in the last 24 months generated $285 million in third quarter revenue, accounting for 28% of our total net sales of $1.02 billion. That's up from 22% a year ago and shows acceleration from 25% in the second quarter, reflecting the payoff from our R&D investments, which reached $145 million this quarter, or 14.2% of sales—exceeding our long-term target range of 12-13%.

Let me highlight the key performers. Leading the pack is our VitaFlex Pro bioresorbable vascular scaffold, or BVS, which earned full FDA PMA approval in late 2023 after compelling 12-month results from the ABSORB IV pivotal trial. It demonstrated 92% target lesion failure-free survival compared to 88% for traditional metallic stents. VitaFlex Pro brought in $112 million in the third quarter, surging 145% year-over-year, thanks to a shift toward higher average selling price procedures. ASP climbed to $4,200 per unit, up 18% sequentially, supported by its fully degradable polymer matrix and AI-optimized deployment features. This is helping us gain ground against established players like Abbott's legacy Absorb BVS and Boston Scientific's Synergy XD, particularly as cardiologists focus on minimizing long-term inflammation for younger patients facing the growing diabetes challenge.

Adding to this is our NeuroPulse neuromodulation platform, a cutting-edge spinal cord stimulator featuring closed-loop adaptive stimulation. It launched in Europe with CE Mark in the first quarter and posted $68 million in third quarter sales, up 210% year-over-year. Adoption in chronic pain management—a global market worth $7.5 billion and expanding at an 8.5% CAGR according to Grand View Research—has been robust. U.S. reimbursement got a boost from CMS's July coverage decision for our burst stimulation waveform, lifting procedural volumes 35% quarter-over-quarter. We've now captured 12% U.S. market share in rechargeable SCS systems, closing in on Medtronic's Intellis and Nevro's HF10.

In robotics, the OrthoBotix system—a compact, AI-powered arm for knee and hip replacements—hit $52 million in third quarter revenue following FDA 510(k) clearance in April, growing 95% year-over-year. With more than 1,200 systems placed to date, attach rates for our PrecisionGuide disposables stand at 22%, with an ASP of $2,800. By targeting high-volume orthopedics, we're challenging Intuitive Surgical's soft-tissue focus and Stryker's Mako, which commands 65% share, but our $1.2 million price point and 20-minute setup time are winning favor.

Breaking it down geographically, the U.S. drove 62% of new product sales at $177 million, up 32% year-over-year, aided by normalizing elective procedures—structural heart volumes rose 15% per Definitive Healthcare—and our fast-track 510(k) approach, securing six approvals year-to-date. EMEA grew 22% to $63 million, overcoming EU MDR hurdles via early VitaFlex Pro compliance; we're active in 14 countries, with Germany and the UK contributing 45% through strong DACH reimbursement. Asia-Pacific jumped 48% to $32 million, powered by China NMPA approval for NeuroPulse in June and partnerships like MicroPort, in a market set for 12% annual growth through 2028. Emerging regions like LATAM added 8% growth via initial OrthoBotix pilots in Brazil.

These achievements stem from our "3-2-1 Innovation Engine": three platforms in Phase III trials, including a TAVR valve rivaling Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien; two tuck-in acquisitions this year, such as a $250 million digital therapeutics deal enhancing our AI capabilities; and one major supply chain shift to address resin constraints. New product gross margins improved 420 basis points to 72.5%, driven by scale and integration at our Galway, Ireland site. Moving ahead, we anticipate these launches fueling 65-70% of our fiscal 2024 organic growth target of 9-11%, backed by a $2.5 billion five-year pipeline that includes GLP-1 compatible continuous glucose monitors to ride the obesity device wave.

In essence, these innovations are transforming our growth trajectory amid patent expirations and biosimilar threats. We're capturing market share and setting up for mid-teens expansion cycle after cycle.

Now, let's talk about gross margin trends and supply chain developments. We posted a third quarter gross margin of 68.4%, expanding 190 basis points year-over-year from 66.5% and 110 basis points from second quarter's 67.3%. This is our best quarterly showing in two years and keeps us on pace for about 250 basis points of full-year growth to roughly 67.8%. That's ahead of med device peers like Medtronic's 65-66% or Boston Scientific's mid-60s, thanks to mix benefits, pricing discipline, and cost reductions.

Product mix added around 120 basis points. Our Cardiovascular segment, now 52% of revenue versus 48% last year, led with mid-teens growth in high-margin structural heart items like next-gen TAVR valves akin to Edwards' Sapien and drug-eluting stents, both over 75% margins. Softer Electrophysiology disposables, similar to Biosense Webster ablation catheters, faced demand normalization post-COVID backlogs, but we countered with premium pricing on AI mapping systems. The overall pivot to capital and implants from basic disposables has been positive, aligning with industry shifts to minimally invasive tech.

Raw material and freight deflation contributed 80 basis points, with medical-grade resins, stainless steel hypotubes, and platinum-iridium alloys down 12-15% sequentially after 2022-2023 shortages. Asia-Pacific freight dropped 20% year-over-year. Multi-year deals with DuPont for Pebax and Heraeus for metals provide stability. FX pressured us by 10 basis points from a stronger euro on European ops, but local sourcing hedged it to under 5 basis points net.

On supply chain, on-time delivery reached 98.2%, up from 94% last year and matching pre-pandemic norms, due to diversification since 2022. In North America, 55% of COGS, we've insourced 30% of components to Costa Rica, cutting reliance on Chinese nitinol frames—echoing Stryker's Latin America strategy—and trimming lead times 40% with margin gains. Asia shifts moved 25% electronics from Shenzhen to Vietnam and Indonesia, dodging U.S.-China tariffs that hit Abbott. Semiconductor lead times for neuromodulation chips, like those in SCS akin to Nevro's HF10, fell to 12 weeks from 28. TSMC mid-tier nodes back up Broadcom.

Europe's Galway plant handles 15% sourcing with MDR advantages, though we're eyeing Carbon Border Adjustment impacts post-2026 with more localization. Cobotic automation covers 40% of stent crimping and catheter lines via Universal Robots and our vision AI, yielding 18% labor gains and scrap from 2.1% to 1.2%. Additive manufacturing pilots with SLM Solutions for ortho implants aim for 10% savings by fiscal 2024 end. Recycled polymers cut Scope 3 emissions 22% without margin hits.

We're allocating $150 million over two years for vertical integration, including a U.S. hypotube facility for 60% control of key parts—Intuitive Surgical-style. This supports 100 basis points annual expansion through fiscal 2025. Q4 margins should hit 68.5-69.0%, with full-year guidance at 68-69%. Inventory at $400 million buffers resin risks or recalls.

Moving on to the trends in our capital equipment versus consumables mix. This razor-and-blade model, like Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci or Medtronic's platforms, is core to our recurring revenue. Capital includes durable systems such as the Aurora Robotic-Assisted Surgery platform, PrecisionFlow Angio cath labs, and OrthoGuide 5.0 navigation suites—priced $1.5 million to $4 million with 7-10 year lives. Consumables are the annuities: single-use instruments, endoscopic kits, guidewires, balloons, bioactive stents, and scaffolds.

For the quarter, we shifted to 68% consumables and 32% capital, from 64%/36% last year—a 400 basis point consumables gain amid procedure rebounds and base expansion. Consumables hit $312 million, up 14% organically and 70% of revenue; capital was $134 million, flat year-over-year post-Aurora ramp comps.

Key drivers: Installed base grew to 5,200 RAS and cath lab units, up 22% from 4,270, with 180 new Aurora placements in Q3, including 45 in centers using AI tissue segmentation. Utilization rose to 87% procedures per system monthly, up 500 basis points, as urology, gyn, and general surgery ORs climbed 18% per our SG&A-aligned tracking. Per-procedure revenue increased 9% to $2,450 via premium FlexiGrip end-effectors with 20% better precision and lower reprocessing.

Tech upgrades helped: Aurora 2.0's haptic feedback and 4K imaging lifted consumables attach by 15% in adopters, a 25% uplift over legacy. PrecisionFlow's EchoGuide integration boosted cath consumables 20%. BioMesh hernia kits could add $50 million annuities by 2025 via degradation tech cutting readmits. Consumables margins hit 82% vs. 65% capital, lifting segment margins 210 basis points to 71%.

By region: U.S. (55%) consumables up 16% on CMS OPPS boosts of 4.2% for RAS; strong Southeast/Midwest Aurora installs with bundles. Europe (25%) grew 8% despite German/French DRGs, offset by 12 UK/Spain Auroras emphasizing 22% shorter stays. Asia-Pacific (15%) soared 25% via China JDAs, India ortho surge, Singapore stent localization beating FX. Rest of World (5%) up 30% in Brazil distributor capitals.

This mix gives 85% 2024 revenue visibility from backlog/base, buffering capital cycles like Stryker's downturns. Targeting 72-75% consumables by 2025 via $250 million capitals in RAS (to 7,000 units), 20 new SKUs like neurovascular coils, and M&A like peptide implants. Risks: RAS semis, Medicare cuts; but 45% premium RAS consumables share fortifies us.

Finally, the impact of our pricing and cost management efforts. Facing reimbursement squeezes, inflation in titanium/polymers, and Asian competition, these drove 250 basis points adjusted gross margin growth to 67.8% from 65.3%, powering over 60% of year-over-year EBITDA rise to $285 million.

Pricing protected ASPs: Structural Heart ASP up 4.2% to $28,500 on AccuFlow transcatheter shift to 35% segment revenue from 22%, adding 180 basis points. Outcomes-based IDN/GPO deals in Electrophysiology—like CryoPulse akin to Medtronic Arctic Front—covered 40% U.S. volume, linking 10-15% pricing to readmits/success (beating by 12%), yielding $18 million extra. Pricing added 3.1% top-line ex-FX, countering 2% CMS IPPS ortho DRG cuts.

U.S. +3.5% ASP via Vizient/Premier; EMEA +2.8% tiered NeuroStim bundles vs. Abbott Infinity DBS; Asia +1.5% via China/India localization/tenders.

Costs saved $120 million run-rate, 65% to bottom line. Supplier consolidation to 320 cut Orthopedics (28% revenue) COGS 5.2% despite 14% titanium spike. Galway Industry 4.0 AI maintenance slashed ortho scrap 22%, throughput 18%—Stryker Mako-scale. Robotics lean Six Sigma dropped assembly 11% to 72.4% margins. R&D steady at 12.1%, SG&A down 7% via ZBB/Bangalore; U.S. labor offset by 15% non-core cuts.

U.S. savings beat 3% Medicare cuts for 280 bps expansion; Europe hit 66% margins vs. peers' 62% despite energy inflation; Asia Suzhou local cut logistics 9%, fueling 22% heart growth.

Forward: $50 million digitization for FDA UDI blockchain, payer bundles with Optum. Sustaining 200+ bps accretion to 70% margins by 2025, backing 12-14% organic growth.

I will now turn the call over to Michael for a review of our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena outlined, we delivered a strong financial performance this quarter. Total net sales reached $1.02 billion, up 12% year-over-year on 10% organic growth, new products, and currency tailwinds. Breaking it down, Cardiovascular drove 52% of revenue with mid-teens gains; Orthopedics and Neuromodulation followed with double-digits.

Expenses were well-controlled: R&D at 14.2% of sales, SG&A down 50 basis points to 24.5% via efficiencies. Operating income rose 22% to $210 million, with adjusted EBITDA at $285 million, a 19% margin—up 180 basis points. Diluted EPS was $1.42, beating consensus by $0.08.

Balance sheet remains solid: $1.8 billion cash, debt-to-EBITDA at 1.8x. We repurchased $100 million in shares and deployed $75 million in capex, focused on Galway expansion.

Guidance: Q4 revenue $1.05-1.08 billion, up 8-11%; full-year organic 9-11%. Gross margins 68-69%; EBITDA margin 19-20%. Risks include FX and volumes, but our pipeline and mix position us well.

Now, I'll turn the call back to Elena for Q&A.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Michael. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On new products, can you elaborate on the competitive dynamics for VitaFlex Pro and any early read on share gains versus Absorb and Synergy XD?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, John. VitaFlex Pro's superior 92% failure-free survival from ABSORB IV is resonating, especially with its degradable matrix reducing inflammation for diabetic patients. We've seen initial share grabs in complex PCI cases, with ASP premium reflecting that. Against Absorb legacy and Synergy, our AI deployment is differentiating—early adopter feedback shows 15% fewer malappositions. Expecting acceleration as we hit more centers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Hi, team. Strong margins—curious about supply chain risks into 2025, especially with potential alloy tariffs or resin volatility. How does the $150 million vertical push factor in?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, Lisa. We've derisked meaningfully—98% on-time delivery, diversified sourcing, and that $150 million gets us to 60% control on hypotubes and resins via the new U.S. fab. CBAM in Europe is modeled at 2-3% cost, but localization counters it. $400 million inventory gives runway; we're confident in 100 bps annual expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
Thanks. For OrthoBotix and Aurora, what's the utilization trajectory and any CTO insights on AI enhancements driving consumables attach?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Mike, thanks. OrthoBotix utilization is tracking 85% post-placement, with AI segmentation cutting setup to 20 minutes and boosting PrecisionGuide pulls to 22%. Aurora 2.0's haptics and 4K are pushing 15% attach uplifts—our vision AI detects tissue variances 25% better than competitors, directly lifting per-procedure revenue. Pilots show 87% system utilization; scaling to 7,000 bases by 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Park with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Park:
Solid guidance—how do pricing/cost initiatives sustain amid reimbursement? Any updates on TAVR pipeline?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Emily, pricing held +3-4% via value-based deals exceeding metrics by 12%, offsetting CMS drags. Cost savings run-rate at $120 million scales with automation. TAVR competitor to Sapien is Phase III, with first-in-human positive; on track for 2026 PMA. These support 12-14% organic and margin path to 70%.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to reiterate our confidence in the long-term growth potential of VitalCore Medical Devices. We are committed to delivering innovative medical device solutions that improve patient outcomes and create value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
